outcome: indications for EPH (uterine rupture, morbidly adherent placenta, placenta previa, uterine atony, postpartum hemorrhage)

maternal complications (wound sepsis, pyrexia, blood transfusion requirements, inotropic support, disseminated intravascular coagulation, bladder injury, acute renal failure, multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, paralytic ileus)
neonatal outcomes (live births, stillbirths, NICU admission, perinatal mortality)
cohort: Women who underwent Emergency Peripartum Hysterectomy (EPH) within 24 hours postpartum at a rural tertiary care center.
finding: Emergency Peripartum Hysterectomy (EPH) occurred in 2.26 per 1,000 deliveries, with previous cesarean section and multiparity identified as key modifiable risk factors for this procedure.
mod_finding: All Emergency Peripartum Hysterectomies in this study followed cesarean deliveries.
